findings.description: Unsafe pickle deserialization in Style.meta property allows arbitrary code execution
findings.code_snippet: return {} if self._meta is None else cast(Dict[str, Any], loads(self._meta))
findings.reasoning: The Style.meta property deserializes pickled data using pickle.loads() without any validation. Since self._meta can contain arbitrary pickled data (set via Style.from_meta() or Style constructor with meta parameter), an attacker can craft malicious pickle payloads that execute arbitrary code when deserialized. This is a classic unsafe deserialization vulnerability (CWE-502) that can lead to remote code execution if untrusted data is processed.

evidence.code_context:
Line 471: The meta property calls pickle.loads(self._meta)
Line 196: In __init__, meta is pickled using pickle.dumps(meta)
Line 247: In from_meta, meta is pickled using pickle.dumps(meta)
Line 520-530: In rich/text.py, apply_meta() calls Style.from_meta(meta) which pickles user-provided meta dictionary

The vulnerability exists because: 1) User-controlled data can be pickled via Style.from_meta() or Style constructor, 2) The pickled data is later deserialized via pickle.loads() in the meta property getter, 3) No validation or sanitization is performed on the pickled data.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: Data flow: User-provided meta dict → pickle.dumps() → stored in self._meta → pickle.loads() when meta property accessed → arbitrary code execution
evidence.notes: This is in vendored rich library code within pip. While the direct attack surface in pip might be limited, any application using this vulnerable version of rich could be affected. The pickle module is inherently unsafe for untrusted data.

findings.description: Standard SSL context creation incorrectly flagged as weak cryptography
findings.reasoning: This code uses Python's standard ssl.create_default_context() which creates a secure SSL/TLS context with safe defaults. This is not weak cryptography - it's proper usage of the SSL library for secure connections. The CodeQL query likely flagged it because it detects SSL-related operations, but this is actually secure standard practice.
